uncertainties.note: Speaker not tagged; role text (personally entrusted with command by Commander Bloodman, distrustful of the Siberian Railway/Izumo after repeated failures) does not match Berkt, who is discussed as a third party two rows later (5910). Left unattributed rather than guessed; likely an unnamed New Federation officer over this operation.

5904 addresses 'Captain Jurgens' by name/rank (locked spelling, character_names_021.json), so that reply is his; the other side of the argument (wants theEND deployed immediately) is unnamed in the table. Plausibly Dominic (established as Jurgens' subordinate who pushes for decisive Anemone/theEND deployment, per review_01666.json), but not asserted since no tag or name appears in these rows.
Source fullwidth 'theEND' (ヽtheヽEND stylised as 〇the〇END, i.e. ｔｈｅＥＮＤ) rendered as 'theEND' to match the already-locked unit name 'Nirvash theEND' (unit_names_014_b.json) rather than 'the END'.

Anemone (named, locked gender female) is upset about being kept out of combat; the other voice (5922, 5924, 5926) is unnamed but its role (worried about reporting her death to Colonel Dewey) matches Dominic's established glossary role as 'Anemone's handler'. Not written into the text since the source does not tag a speaker.
大佐 (taisa) for Dewey rendered 'Colonel' (no prior corpus rank lock found for Dewey via grep); flag for orchestrator to confirm against any later scene that fixes his rank.

The cloaking 'Overman' (5934-5937) is never named in this slice; kept as 'that Overman' rather than guessing it is 'Blackmail' from the task description, since the source text itself never names it here.
'イズモ隣' (Izumo squad/unit) rendered 'the Izumo', matching the ship-name-as-unit convention already used for Jurgens' ship (batch_01666.json: 'Izumo, prepare to withdraw!').
